title: Introducing Supervibes: A Native Mac App That Builds iOS Projects Autonomously
summary: Build native Swift apps, use Superwall seamlessly, and go from idea in your head to App Store in record time
body_text: AI coding tools are everywhere. But when it comes to iOS developers, the tools, and results, your mileage can vary. Some of the tools aren't native, nor do they produce native results, and while we are big fans of React Native, Expo, and Flutter — we wondered if there was a place for us to make something specifically for native iOS development. That's one of the problems we set out to solve with Supervibes . It's a Mac app built from the ground up to understand Xcode, SwiftUI, and the realities of shipping apps to the App Store. Plus, it comes bundled with our in-house MCPs to make the whole process of building, testing, and shipping feel smooth. Monetization is built-in, as our Superwall MCP can get your paywalls showing out of the box. Over the past two months, we've been quietly building and testing it. Today, we're excited to finally share it with the world. Download it now! All native and built for iOS development Most "AI pair programmers" were designed for web or backend workflows. And, over the last few years, they've become extremely good at it. Creating apps is more than writing code, though. Most tools likely require the terminal, or perhaps don't understand simulators or devices, and have minimal awareness of what makes iOS development unique. While we are huge fans of tools like Claude Code (in fact, Supervibes uses Claude under the hood), we wanted to make something for those who aren't quite familiar with the full toolchain yet. Things like provisioning profiles, signing, bundle IDs, or even your Info.plist are critical components of the iOS landscape, but agents can start to falter a bit when it comes to dealing with them. Supervibes changes that. It's a native Mac app that works directly with any Xcode project, new or existing. From the developer's perspective, there are no extensions, no plugins, and no setup scripts. You can use it with or without Xcode open. Just drag in a project or start from scratch, and you're ready to build. Supervibes is ready to go with a new project or your existing ones. Our tweaks are what make Supervibes different Supervibes was designed with one goal: to make progress toward making iOS development actually autonomous. When you open it, you're greeted by a chat interface. There aren't a ton of controls, buttons, or decisions to make. And, that's on purpose. We wanted it to feel like using iMessage. You're just chatting: Supervibe's chat interface is all you need to build apps. Earlier I mentioned our custom MCPs, and that's what powers critical services of Supervibes: 🛠️ Build MCP — Compiles directly to your simulator or device. 🤑 Superwall MCP — Integrates Superwall's SDK automatically. In other words it can design, build, test, and integrate and all without ever leaving the app. Plus, we can get you started the right way. Our starter project is an opinionated foundation that takes the busywork out of building production-ready apps, so you can focus on what makes your idea special. Once you start a new project or open an existing one, Supervibes helps get things in motion. It doesn't just make suggestions. Instead, we geared it to run builds, edit configuration files via xcodegen, and can even fix its own build errors in real time by reading the logs and trying again. It can discover connected devices, build to them, and handle code signing automatically. From your end, that frees you up to simply type out what you want, the tweaks you need, or the direction the app should take. Supervibes will get out of your way, and most importantly — take care of the other things that can get in your way, and simply execute on your ideas. Wrapping up Supervibes is not a plugin, not a terminal tool, and not a code editor. It's a vibe coder — a standalone Mac app that understands how iOS apps actually get made, built, and shipped. To wrap up, Supervibes... 🚀 Works with any new or existing Xcode project 📱 Builds directly to simulator or device 💻 Runs with or without Xcode open 💰 Focused on shipping and monetizing apps faster ✨ Onboarding and analytics out of the box 🧩 Built-in Superwall integration 🧠 Fixes its own build errors automatically That means that all you need is: Xcode installed And a Claude Pro or Max subscription Supervibes is just getting started. We have several new MCPs coming out soon, which will put our industry-leading knowledge over paywalls, conversions, and best practices to practical use. Get started today!

title: What Is a Passport? Types, Uses & How to Get One
summary: What is a passport and why do you need one? Learn its types, key functions, and step-by-step tips to get yours before your next international trip.
body_text: Picture this: you’ve booked your dream flight, packed your bags, and you’re buzzing with excitement, only to realize you have no idea whether your passport is still valid, or whether you even have one. It happens more often than you’d think. Whether you’re planning your very first trip overseas or you’re a seasoned traveler brushing up on the basics, understanding what a passport is and how it works is genuinely one of the most important things you can do before going global. If you’re also thinking about how to work abroad from Indonesia , a valid passport is literally step one. Let’s break it all down in plain language so you walk away feeling completely confident. List of Content Toggle What Is a Passport, Exactly? A passport is an official government-issued travel document that proves two things: your identity and your nationality. Think of it as your golden ticket to crossing international borders legally. Without it, most countries simply won’t let you in. Beyond just getting you through border control, a passport is widely accepted as a primary form of identification around the world. It carries your full name, date of birth, photo, nationality, and a unique passport number that authorities use to track your travel history. 1. The Core Purpose of a Passport At its heart, a passport does three key things: Proves who you are to foreign governments and immigration officers. Confirms your citizenship , which determines what rights and protections your home country can offer you abroad. Enables re-entry back into your own country after traveling overseas. No other single document carries all three of those functions at once. That’s exactly why it’s so powerful and so essential. 2. What Information Does a Passport Contain? Open up any standard passport and you’ll find a data page packed with key details: Full legal name Date and place of birth Passport number Issue and expiry dates Nationality and country of issue A Machine Readable Zone (MRZ) , which is the two lines of coded text at the bottom of your photo page that scanners read instantly Modern passports also contain a biometric chip embedded in the cover, which stores a digital version of your photo and fingerprints. This makes them significantly harder to forge. Types of Passports You Should Know About Not all passports are created equal. Depending on who you are and why you’re traveling, you might be issued a different type of passport. Here’s a quick rundown. 1. Regular (Ordinary) Passport This is the standard passport most people carry. It’s issued to ordinary citizens for personal travel, tourism, business trips, and study abroad. If you’re planning to study abroad as an international student , this is almost certainly the type you’ll need. 2. Official Passport Issued to government employees traveling for official state business. It’s not available to the general public, and it signals to foreign authorities that the holder is traveling on behalf of their government. 3. Diplomatic Passport Reserved for diplomats, ambassadors, and senior government officials. Holders often receive special treatment at borders and may be exempt from certain customs inspections under international law. 4. Emergency or Temporary Passport Lost your passport while already abroad? This is your lifeline. Emergency passports are issued quickly by embassies or consulates and are usually valid for a short period, just enough to get you home safely. Why Your Passport Matters Beyond Just Traveling Here’s something many people overlook: your passport isn’t just a travel document. It carries real-world weight in a variety of situations. 1. It Unlocks Visa Applications Applying for a visa to another country? Your passport number, issue date, and expiry date are the foundation of almost every visa application form. The strength of your passport, meaning how many countries you can enter without a prior visa, also varies by nationality. 2. It’s a Universal ID Banks, embassies, foreign employers, and universities abroad routinely ask for your passport as proof of identity. It carries more international credibility than a national ID card in most contexts. 3. It Protects You Abroad Your passport links you to your home country’s consular protection network. If you’re in trouble overseas, your embassy uses your passport to verify your citizenship and provide assistance. This is especially relevant if you’re part of the broader Indonesian diaspora living and working far from home. How to Get a Passport: A Step-by-Step Overview The exact process differs by country, but the general framework is pretty consistent across the board. Here’s what the journey typically looks like. 1. Gather Your Documents Before you even walk into a passport office, collect the essentials: Proof of citizenship (birth certificate or existing citizenship document) A valid national identity card Recent passport-sized photos meeting official specifications Completed application form (usually downloadable from your country’s immigration website) Any supporting documents if applying for a child or renewing an existing passport 2. Submit Your Application Head to your nearest immigration office or passport-issuing authority. In many countries, you can now start the process online and only visit in person for biometric data capture (your photo and fingerprints). Book your appointment early, especially during peak travel seasons, because slots fill up fast. 3. Pay the Required Fee Passport fees vary depending on your country, the type of passport, and how quickly you need it. Standard processing is cheaper; expedited or rush processing costs more. Check the current rates on your government’s official immigration portal. 4. Wait for Processing Standard processing can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks. If you have a confirmed travel date coming up soon, apply for expedited processing or visit in person and explain your situation. Always give yourself a buffer, ideally several weeks before your travel date. 5. Check Validity Before Every Trip Many countries require your passport to be valid for at least six months beyond your intended stay. Even if your passport technically hasn’t expired, you could be denied boarding if it’s too close to the expiry date. Always check before you book, not after. Tips to Keep Your Passport Safe Losing your passport abroad is one of the most stressful experiences a traveler can face. A few simple habits can save you a world of trouble. Make digital and physical copies of the data page and store them separately from the original. Use a passport holder or hidden travel pouch to avoid pickpocketing in busy tourist areas. Never hand your passport to anyone unofficial, especially at hotels or travel agencies, without understanding exactly why they need it. Store your passport in the hotel safe when you don’t need it for the day. Report a lost or stolen passport to both local police and your nearest embassy immediately. And if your travels extend to cruise trips, note that passport requirements can be slightly different depending on the itinerary. Check out our guide on requirements for international cruise travel to make sure you’re fully prepared. See Also: How to Find a Job Abroad: A Practical Guide Your passport is more than just a little booklet. It’s your key to the world, your proof of identity across borders, and your connection back home no matter where life takes you. Whether you’re applying for the first time, renewing an old one, or helping a family member get theirs sorted, now you know exactly what a passport is and why it matters. Take care of it, keep it updated, and let it open doors you never imagined. title: Core Scientific Appoints Mark Adams to Board of Directors
summary: Proven Technology Executive Brings Track Record of Scaling and Transforming Global Businesses MIAMI--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Core Scientific, Inc.…...
body_text: Core Scientific Appoints Mark Adams to Board of Directors July 29, 2026 5:50 am EDT Download as PDF Proven Technology Executive Brings Track Record of Scaling and Transforming Global Businesses MIAMI--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Core Scientific, Inc. (Nasdaq: CORZ) (“Core Scientific” or the “Company”), a leader in digital infrastructure for high-density colocation (“HDC”), today announced the appointment of Mark W. Adams to its Board of Directors, effective immediately. With the addition of Mr. Adams, Core Scientific’s Board will expand to seven directors. Mr. Adams brings over three decades of technology leadership experience across the AI infrastructure, semiconductors, storage, digital media, and enterprise hardware industries. Most recently, he served as President and Chief Executive Officer of Penguin Solutions, Inc. (formerly SMART Global Holdings, Inc.) from 2020 until 2026. During his tenure, he led the company through a multi-year repositioning toward AI infrastructure solutions, including memory solutions and IT services serving enterprise and hyperscale customers. Prior to Penguin, Mr. Adams spent ten years at Micron Technology, Inc., where he held a series of senior leadership roles, including serving as President for four years. Mr. Adams currently serves on the boards of directors of Seagate Technology Holdings Public Limited Company, where he has served as a director since 2024, and Cadence Design Systems, Inc., where he has served as a director since 2015. Mr. Adams holds an MBA from Harvard University and a B.A. from Boston College. “Mark brings an exceptional combination of technology leadership and operational expertise to our Board,” said Adam Sullivan, Chief Executive Officer of Core Scientific. “Throughout his career, he has successfully scaled complex global businesses, led strategic transformations and helped companies capitalize on shifts in demand for computing infrastructure. His deep experience across AI infrastructure, semiconductors and data storage will be highly relevant as we continue expanding our high-density data center platform and strengthening our foundation for growth." “Core Scientific is operating at the forefront of the AI infrastructure market, developing the critical capacity needed to support the growth of advanced computing,” said Mark Adams. “I am excited to join the Board and support the important work already underway to expand the Company’s platform, deepen customer relationships and deliver durable value for shareholders.” About Core Scientific, Inc. Core Scientific is a leader in designing, building and operating large scale, purpose-built data centers for high-density colocation (“HDC”) services. Core Scientific operates facilities for high-density colocation services serving artificial intelligence-related (“AI”) workloads and is a premier provider of digital infrastructure and services to its third-party customers. The majority of the Company's revenue is derived from high-density colocation services, with the remainder derived from earning digital assets for the Company's own account and from digital asset mining hosting services. The Company is in the process of repurposing its remaining mining facilities to support its high-density colocation services business as circumstances allow. Core Scientific’s facilities are located in Alabama (1), Georgia (2), Kentucky (1), North Carolina (1), North Dakota (1), Oklahoma (1) and Texas (4). To learn more, visit www.corescientific.com . title: What is an automatic time tracker?
summary: An automatic time tracker records where your time goes with no timers and no manual entry. How the three kinds work - app loggers, screen-based journals, and AI memory tools - and how to pick.
body_text: An automatic time tracker is software that records where your time goes without you starting timers, filling timesheets, or tagging anything. You work; it watches; at the end of the day there is a record. The category exists because the manual version fails the same way for everyone: you forget to start the timer, then forget to stop it, then stop using the tool. The three kinds 1. App and window loggers. These record which application and window title is in the foreground, and build charts from it. ActivityWatch (free, open source, cross-platform) is the reference implementation; RescueTime and Rize add cloud dashboards, productivity scores, and coaching on top. Strength: extremely lightweight, works everywhere. Limit: the output is app names - “Chrome, 5h 12m” - which tells you where your windows were, not what you did. 2. Screen-based journals. These look at the screen itself and reconstruct the work. Dayflow (free, open source, Mac) records one frame every 10 seconds and has AI write a readable timeline - “Implementing OAuth token refresh, 9:04-9:48” - because the same Chrome window can be code review or cat videos, and only the screen contents know which. Strength: the output is an actual account of your day in sentences. Limit: Mac-only, and it sees only what happens on that screen. 3. AI memory reconstructors. Tools like Timely’s “Memory” record app activity to a cloud timeline, then help you (or an AI) assemble billable time entries from it afterward. Aimed at teams and client billing rather than personal awareness. What separates the good ones Where the data lives. Your complete working history is sensitive. Some tools keep it on your machine (Dayflow, ActivityWatch, Qbserve, Memtime); most cloud tools process it on their servers. If the record is intimate, local should be the default. What the output is. Charts answer “how much”; a journal answers “what happened.” Pick by the question you actually ask at 6pm - for most individuals it is where did my day go , which charts cannot answer. Idle cost. An all-day tool must be invisible: think ~100MB of RAM and under 1% CPU ( the battery math is here ). Price and openness. The field splits into subscriptions ($7-25/month for RescueTime, Rize, Timing, Timely) and free open source (ActivityWatch, Dayflow). Open source also means the privacy claims are auditable rather than promised. The short version If you want cross-platform app statistics, ActivityWatch is the free classic. If you bill clients by the hour, look at Timing or Memtime. If the question is what you actually did all day, answered in plain sentences with everything staying on your Mac - that is exactly what Dayflow is: the only Mac option that is fully automatic, AI-powered, 100% local, and free at the same time. The full comparison across nine trackers is here .
